title: The Empire That Wrote in Knots
hook: The Incas ruled 10 million people without writing a single sentence on paper.

scenes.text: The Inca Empire stretched two thousand five hundred miles across the Andes mountains, governing ten million subjects.
scenes.imagePrompt: Monumental Inca stone fortress terrace at Sacsayhuaman with massive fitted polygonal megalithic stones under blue Andean skies. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: The Inca Empire stretched two thousand five hundred miles across the Andes mountains, governing ten million subjects.

scenes.text: Yet remarkably, they never developed a written alphabet on paper or parchment—instead, their entire bureaucracy ran on 'quipus'.
scenes.imagePrompt: Close-up of an ancient Inca quipu: a thick primary wool cord with dozens of colored cotton string pendants hanging down. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Yet remarkably, they never developed a written alphabet on paper or parchment—instead, their entire bureaucracy ran on 'quipus'.

scenes.text: A quipu consisted of a main cord with hundreds of dangling colored llama-wool strings tied with intricate clusters of knots.
scenes.imagePrompt: Detailed view of various knot types: figure-eight knots, long spiral knots, and simple knots tied in dyed alpaca wool strings. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: A quipu consisted of a main cord with hundreds of dangling colored llama-wool strings tied with intricate clusters of knots.

scenes.text: Using a decimal base-10 system, string color, spin direction, and knot spacing recorded army troop counts, gold taxes, and granary stores.
scenes.imagePrompt: Stone administrative storehouse in Cuzco with organized rows of rolled quipu string archives resting in carved wall niches. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Using a decimal base-10 system, string color, spin direction, and knot spacing recorded army troop counts, gold taxes, and granary stores.

scenes.text: Official masters called 'quipucamayocs' could read complex histories, tax debts, and royal decrees simply by sliding fingers across the cords.

scenes.voicedText: Official masters called 'quipucamayocs' could read complex histories, tax debts, and royal decrees simply by sliding fingers across the cords.
